subject: Materials Science
title: Pourbaix Diagrams: Maps of Corrosion
description: One-minute skill: Pourbaix Diagrams: Maps of Corrosion.

hook.text: Is your iron pipe corroding, passivated, or immune? A single diagram tells you — if you know pH and voltage.

buildup.text: A Pourbaix diagram plots electrode potential vs pH, showing regions of immunity, corrosion, and passivation.

discovery.text: In the immunity region, the metal is thermodynamically stable — no driving force for corrosion exists.

twist.text: Thermodynamics says if corrosion can happen — kinetics decides how fast. A Pourbaix diagram shows possibility, not rate.

climax.text: Corrosion engineers use Pourbaix diagrams to choose coatings, cathodic protection levels, and water chemistry.

punchline.text: One diagram maps every state a metal can be in — corroding, protected, or safe.

quiz.question: What does a Pourbaix diagram show?
options: The strength of a metal at different temperatures
Regions of immunity, corrosion, and passivation as a function of potential and pH
The rate of corrosion over time
